questions.q: What actually defines whether something is a "client" or a "server"?
options: Whether it has a keyboard and screen attached
Its role in a given conversation: whoever initiates a request is the client, whoever answers is the server
The brand of operating system it runs
The physical size of the hardware
questions.explain: Client and server are roles in a request/response conversation, not fixed categories of hardware. The same machine can be either, depending on who's initiating.

questions.q: A developer's laptop normally browses the web as a client. Under what circumstance could that same laptop act as a server?
options: Only if its hard drive is physically removed
If it's running software that another machine connects to and sends requests to
Only after installing a second operating system
Never — a laptop can only ever be a client
questions.explain: Role depends on behavior, not hardware category. If the laptop is running a service that a colleague's machine sends requests to, the laptop is acting as a server for that conversation.

questions.q: What is the basic pattern that nearly all client-server communication follows?
options: The server initiates contact and the client responds
The client sends a request, the server performs the work and sends back a response
Both sides send requests simultaneously with no response expected
The client and server never communicate directly
questions.explain: The request/response pattern is the basic shape: the client asks for something, the server does the necessary work, and sends the answer back.

questions.q: Why is server hardware typically configured differently than a typical client machine (more RAM, more CPU cores, redundant storage)?
options: Because clients are not allowed to have more than 8GB of RAM
There is no real difference in typical configuration
Because servers need a bigger screen for the user
Because a server may need to reliably answer many simultaneous client requests, often unattended
questions.explain: Because a server often answers many clients at once and runs unattended for long stretches, it's typically built with more capacity and redundancy than a client machine.

questions.q: At Northbridge Retail, a checkout terminal requests a price and stock check from a data center server, and later syncs sales totals to a reporting server. What role is the checkout terminal playing in both cases?
options: Client in both cases, since it initiates each request
Server in both cases
Neither role applies to checkout terminals
Client for the price check, server for the sync
questions.explain: In both interactions, the checkout terminal is the one initiating the request, which makes it the client each time — even though the requests go to different servers for different purposes.
